data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Kandarpa is the god of love and desire. He is the embodiment of passionate love and is depicted as a young man with the power to make anyone fall in love with him. Kandarpa is also known as Kamadeva and is the son of Lord Indra and his wife, Indrani. The name Kandarpa carries the meaning “Cupid, God of Love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi. Parents who choose Kandarpa usually hope their child will grow to embody cupid, god of love and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kandarpa total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Kandarpa, also known as Cupid in Western mythology, is a celebrated god of love in Hinduism. He is depicted holding a bow and arrow, which he uses to shoot arrows of passion and desire into the hearts of individuals to ignite their romantic feelings. This god of amour is often invoked by those seeking love, romance, or passionate relationships in their lives. Adding the name Kandarpa to a child's name is seen as a blessing for ensuring a loving and romantic connection in their lives.
data.spiritual_significance: Kandarpa represents the divine power of love and passion that exists in the universe. It is believed that his energy can help individuals connect on a deeper level, and foster strong, meaningful relationships. The spiritual significance of the name Kandarpa includes evoking the divine energy of love and passion to enrich one's personal relationships, and inspiring individuals to cultivate love and compassion in their hearts and in their relationships with others. In this way, the name Kandarpa serves as a reminder of the importance of love and passion in the spiritual journey of self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kandarpa represents the intense, passionate and fiery nature of love. It is believed to be the name of the Hindu god of love, Kama Deva, who wields the powerful flower arrow, Mohini Manas, to ignite love in the hearts of beings.
